what_happened.line: The town's entire finance department is turning over at once, with a new finance director due to start amid interim coverage.
The finance committee voted unanimously to send its completed master planning committee questionnaire responses to the steering committee.
The town manager recommended dropping a partial roof repair project from the town meeting warrant, routing it through the normal capital planning process instead.
The committee continued questioning a reported gap between school spending and the current fiscal year's budget baseline, without resolving it.
The committee set an October date to review the first-quarter Munis report and pushed a review of town finance policies to November.

why_it_matters: A full turnover in the finance office, including the director, payroll/benefits administrator and assistant accountant, touches how the town's books, payroll and every board's budget requests move through the fall town meeting season.
Dropping the roof repair article means voters will not see that item on the warrant; the funding instead stays attached to a prior appropriation for reappropriation through capital planning.
The unresolved school budget discrepancy is part of the reconciliation work that residents' questions about school funding levels depend on.
watch_next: October 20: new finance director Katie McKenna starts
October 23: finance committee reviews the Q1 FY26 Munis report
